about.title: Danville Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Danville sees a steady share of injury crashes tied to its busiest corridors — I-680 in both directions and Camino Tassajara among them. Public records show 102 injury collisions and 134 people hurt in the most recent reporting year, with Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing more reported activity than other times. Whether you were rear-ended near an I-680 interchange or sideswiped crossing Camino Tassajara, the aftermath can feel disorienting — medical visits, insurance calls, missed work. LawProactive isn't a law firm; we're a free service that connects injured Danville residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened and explain options under California law. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Reaching out early can help make sure evidence from the scene, medical records, and witness accounts are preserved before they're lost or memories fade.

whyChoose.title: Why Danville Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: California's Filing Deadline Is Closer Than You Think
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the crash date to file a claim, but if a government entity (like a road authority) is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help identify which deadline applies to your situation.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly responsible for the crash — your recovery is simply adjusted to reflect your share of fault. An independent attorney can help make sure your percentage of fault is fairly assessed.

items.title: No Cap Means Your Pain and Suffering Still Count
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases. Before speaking with the other driver's insurer or giving a recorded statement, it helps to understand how those damages are calculated.

items.question: I was in a crash near the I-680/Camino Tassajara area — what should I do first?
items.answer: Seek medical attention even if you feel okay, since some injuries surface days later. Try to document the scene with photos and get contact information from any witnesses. Avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company until you've spoken with an independent attorney.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Danville car accident?
items.answer: In California, you generally have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. That timeline can be much shorter — sometimes just six months — if a government entity, such as a county or state road agency, was involved. It's worth checking your specific timeline sooner rather than later.

items.question: Will it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney in our network — we're not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys who take injury cases typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
